newsitem.title: USA: Curry to challenge Conn. Gov. Rowland - report.
newsitem.headline: Curry to challenge Conn. Gov. Rowland - report.

text.p: Former state Comptroller William E. Curry, Jr., a Democrat, formally announced his candidacy for governor, the Hartford Courant reported Wednesday.
Curry, 45, was the Democrats' nominee in 1994 when he lost to Republican John Rowland.
He is the first of the state's well-known Democrats to officially announce his candidacy in a field that could grow to eight contenders, the Courant said.
"I'm in it it stay. I'm in it to win," Curry was quoted as saying.
Curry, who has been teaching at Yale University, said he would focus on cutting property taxes, boosting spending for education, helping cities and protecting the environment.
Other prominent Democrats who are considering a run for governor in 1998 are House Speaker Thomas Ritter, U.S. Rep. Barbara Kennelly, and Bridgeport Mayor Joseph Ganim.
Political analysts expect the race to be the most expensive in state history.
Rowland's advisors think he can raise as much as $7 million, the Courant said.
Ritter said the Democratic candidate needs $5 million to mount a successful challenge.
